text:
maria: Seeing p95 spike on attention paths for seq>=1536 on canary — flash-fuse variant 2.x slower than 1.x when KV-prefetch is enabled. p99 roughly doubled. cc @samir @chen
samir: Can you paste the before/after numbers?
maria: sure, run summary (canary vs baseline):
```
seq | baseline p95 | baseline p99 | canary p95 | canary p99
512 | 18ms         | 28ms         | 20ms       | 31ms
1024| 34ms         | 54ms         | 38ms       | 60ms
1536| 48ms         | 82ms         | 92ms      | 170ms
2048| 76ms         | 138ms        | 140ms     | 260ms
```
chen: Whoa for 1536+ that's large. Any kernel-chooser logs?
maria: pasted kernel-selector snippet:
```
[2026-06-01T12:01:10Z] req=0x7f choose_kernel: seq=1536 kv_prefetch=true scores={flash-fuse=0.62, flash-paged=0.55, flash-attn=0.48}
[2026-06-01T12:01:10Z] req=0x7f selected=flash-fuse reason=heuristic_score
[2026-06-01T12:01:10Z] req=0x7f batches=3 microbatch_size=32
```
nate: I ran nsys on the canary host — lots of tiny kernels + memcpy bursts. Looks like batching delay shortened and we flush more microbatches.
samir: Which heuristic change touched batch delay? PR #1428 adjusted max_batch_delay/ms to 1 (was 4) and pref weight to favor lower latency.
chen: I can repro locally with kv_prefetch=true; flash-fuse triggers more L2 evictions due to stride and KV copy pattern. KV cache miss rate x3.
maria: Bisect started to narrow the reg: running perf-bisect on canary between commits ff099... -> ff9c3
ci-bot: perf-bisect job queued: job_id=bb-1765432135
nate: Workaround: forcing kernel preference to ['flash-fuse-v1','flash-paged'] in runtime config mitigates. Applying to canary now.
infra-bot: runtime override applied to canary group: kernel_order=[flash-fuse-v1,flash-paged]
maria: After override p95 back to ~50ms for seq1536, p99 ~88ms. Regression mitigated on canary.
samir: Bisect result: commit ff2a7b4 (heuristic: batch delay + preference change) is the culprit. I'll open revert PR + add guard for kv_prefetch.
chen: Also proposing we add runtime metrics: kernel_switch_rate per-request and kv_miss_rate histograms; alert if kernel churn > 5/sec or kv_miss_rate spike.
maria: Good. I'll attach repro script and nsys traces to the issue. Thanks all :thumbsup:
